root_cause.text: The `nh_group_v4_update` function was only called when replacing an AF_INET nexthop with an AF_INET6 nexthop, missing the reverse direction (AF_INET6 to AF_INET), causing the `has_v4` flag in nexthop groups to become stale when a nexthop's family changes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (oldi->family == AF_INET && newi->family == AF_INET6)` to `if (oldi->family != newi->family)`, explicitly addressing that the original code only handled one direction of family change. The CVE description confirms that when an IPv6 nexthop is replaced with an IPv4 nexthop, the `has_v4` flag remains false, allowing IPv6 routes to be incorrectly attached to groups containing only AF_INET members, which subsequently causes `nexthop_fib6_nh()` to return NULL and trigger a NULL pointer dereference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Generalize nexthop family mismatch detection to handle all family transitions, not just IPv4 to IPv6 replacements.
intent_record.what: Updated comment to generalize from IPv4-to-IPv6 replacement to any family mismatch, and changed the conditional from checking specifically `oldi->family == AF_INET && newi->family == AF_INET6` to checking `oldi->family != newi->family`.
intent_record.how: The change expands the scope of family mismatch handling to cover all cases where old and new nexthops have different address families (not just IPv4→IPv6), ensuring that IPv4 indication updates are applied whenever a nexthop is replaced with one of a different family, regardless of the specific family combination.

candidates.rationale: This condition only checks for AF_INET to AF_INET6 transitions, missing the reverse direction (AF_INET6 to AF_INET). This causes the `has_v4` flag update logic to be skipped when a nexthop changes from IPv6 to IPv4, leaving the flag stale in nexthop groups.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional statement only checks for the AF_INET to AF_INET6 transition direction, missing the reverse case where a nexthop changes from AF_INET6 to AF_INET. This causes the `nh_group_v4_update` function to not be called when the family changes in the opposite direction, leaving the `has_v4` flag stale in nexthop groups. The condition needs to be generalized to detect all family mismatches between old and new nexthop families, not just the IPv4-to-IPv6 direction.

Author: Ido Schimmel <idosch@nvidia.com>

    ipv4: nexthop: Correctly update nexthop group when replacing a nexthop

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `nh_group_v4_update()` function (lines 967-981) which correctly recalculates the `has_v4` flag by iterating through all nexthops in a group and checking if any have `family == AF_INET`. The function is then called in `replace_nexthop_single()` (lines 1007-1016) when replacing an IPv4 nexthop with an IPv6 nexthop. The code iterates over all groups that contain the replaced nexthop via `list_for_each_entry(nhge, &old->grp_list, nh_list)` and updates their `has_v4` flags. This fix addresses the root cause: the `has_v4` flag is now properly updated when a nexthop's family changes. While the commit message acknowledges it only handles the AF_INET to AF_INET6 direction ('Avoid wasting cycles by only performing the update in case an IPv4 nexthop is replaced by an IPv6 nexthop'), this is the fix being introduced in this commit, not a bug in it.
